source_name: Profesia.cz – Czech job portal (Prague IT)
why_relevant: Alma Career/Profesia network board with strong SK-CZ overlap; useful for spotting cross-border shared-service hiring for CZ bank platforms and for vendor implementation partners staffing CZ projects.

source_name: LinkedIn Jobs / company pages – Czech Republic banking & vendor roles
why_relevant: Richest single source for both vendor-product-named vacancies at CZ banks and employee skill profiles (people listing 'Temenos T24', 'Vynamic', 'Way4', 'Mambu' at a Czech employer), which together date a deployment. Vendor company pages (Temenos, Mambu) also expose CZ-located roles implying local delivery.

source_name: Česká spořitelna GitHub organisation
why_relevant: Public repos and SDKs of the bank that ran the first CZ REST open-banking API; commit history, dependency manifests and API specs reveal the underlying platform, integration partners and technology direction without any communications gatekeeper.

source_name: ČSOB GitHub organisation (incl. paymentgateway repo)
why_relevant: ČSOB publishes its payment-gateway eAPI documentation and POS merchant API publicly; the spec reveals card schemes, wallet integrations (Apple Pay, Google Pay), BNPL partner (mallpay) and processing behaviour — direct evidence of the acquiring/processing stack.

source_name: Komerční banka GitHub organisation (komercka)
why_relevant: KB's public repos accompany its API programme; useful for confirming the tech stack of a bank publicly known to be running a large transformation, and for identifying integration partners via contributors and dependencies.

source_name: cz-banking-psd2 – community list of Czech bank developer portals (GitHub)
why_relevant: A maintained index mapping every Czech bank to its developer portal URL — the single best snowball seed for enumerating CZ bank API docs, sandboxes and the platform vendors behind them.

source_name: COBS – Czech Standard for Open Banking (Czech Banking Association, GitHub)
why_relevant: The technical form of the CZ open-banking standard maintained by the ČBA working group; issue threads and contributor affiliations reveal which banks and vendors staff the standardisation effort — a partnership signal invisible in press material.

source_name: apiportal.cz – Czech banking API portal aggregator
why_relevant: Local-language aggregator of CZ bank API portals; gives current status of each bank's PSD2/premium APIs and is the natural entry point for enumerating developer portals in Czech.

source_name: Česká národní banka developer portal
why_relevant: Regulator-run developer portal with guides for PSD2 banking APIs and registry data; establishes the technical baseline every CZ bank must meet and often names the market conventions vendors must implement.

source_name: Komerční banka API / PSD2 developer portal
why_relevant: KB's public API catalogue and sandbox; endpoint naming, auth flows and SDK artefacts are strong tells about the underlying core/integration platform and any API-management vendor in use.

source_name: ČSOB developer portal
why_relevant: ČSOB's developer hub; combined with its public paymentgateway repo it exposes the acquiring/wallet integration set and API-management layer of a bank publicly undergoing a core transformation (Camunda-based orchestration reported).

source_name: Erste Group / Česká spořitelna developer portal
why_relevant: Group-level developer portal covering the ČS APIs; group-wide API design and any shared platform vendor choices propagate to the CZ entity, so this is a leading indicator for ČS technology decisions.

source_name: Air Bank developer portal
why_relevant: PPF-group challenger bank's API portal; Air Bank is a frequent early adopter, so its API surface and registration flow reveal the platform and identity stack used across the PPF banking assets.

source_name: MONETA Money Bank API portal
why_relevant: MONETA's API portal; even sparse documentation reveals the API-gateway product and versioning conventions, and changes there track the bank's ongoing platform modernisation.

source_name: Raiffeisenbank CZ developer portal
why_relevant: RB's PSD2/open-banking developer site; documents the bank's API standard adherence (COBS/Berlin Group) and exposes the integration layer behind it.

source_name: Partners Banka open banking API documentation
why_relevant: Newest CZ bank licence — a greenfield build, so its API surface is the clearest available fingerprint of which modern core/banking-as-a-service vendor a new CZ entrant selected.

source_name: IT Trendy – Česká spořitelna's tech community portal
why_relevant: Bank-run engineering content portal: articles, interviews with ČS engineering leaders, meetup recordings and an IT event calendar. Engineers describing their stack in public is the closest thing to a Czech bank tech blog, and the event calendar snowballs into vendor-sponsored meetups.

source_name: Kariéra Česká spořitelna – IT positions
why_relevant: Bank's own career site carries the unfiltered version of ads (often more technical than the job-board copy) and lists team/tribe names that map to internal platform programmes.

source_name: Kariéra Air Bank – open positions
why_relevant: Air Bank ads name concrete stacks (Java, Python, Go, AI engineering) and team missions; a PPF-group challenger's hiring pattern is an early indicator of platform bets that later reach Home Credit/other group assets.

source_name: VímVíc.cz – employer profiles and vacancies (e.g. ČSOB)
why_relevant: CZ employer-review/career aggregator; consolidates a bank's vacancies plus employee commentary, giving both hiring signals and soft internal-organisation detail (team names, tooling complaints) that hint at platform programmes.

source_name: Glassdoor – Diebold Nixdorf Czech Republic / Prague pages
why_relevant: Confirms Diebold Nixdorf's CZ engineering/service footprint (Prague and Plzeň) and surfaces role descriptions naming ATM software platforms (Vynamic/Vista) — direct evidence of who services CZ self-service fleets, corroborating the ČSOB self-service partnership.

source_name: Vendor career sites with CZ-located roles (Temenos, Mambu, NCR Atleos)
why_relevant: A vendor advertising a Prague-based implementation consultant or a CZ-language support role is a strong tell that a live Czech client engagement exists before any joint announcement; Workday job feeds are structured and location-filterable.

source_name: openbankingtracker.com – Czech Republic provider index
why_relevant: Third-party index of ~165 CZ providers with their API/developer-portal status; an efficient way to enumerate the long tail of CZ banks, credit unions and PSPs whose developer artefacts should be watched.

source_name: CzechCrunch (cc.cz) – bank IT/technology coverage
why_relevant: CZ tech-business outlet that interviews bank IT leadership and reports headcount/stack detail (e.g. ČS's 1,500 IT staff, launch of IT Trendy); good pointer to engineering artefacts and to people worth tracking.

source_name: Shoptet Doplňky – kategorie Platby (payment add-on marketplace)
why_relevant: Shoptet is the dominant CZ e-shop platform (tens of thousands of merchants). Its Platby add-on category is a live, enumerable registry of which payment gateways/PSPs are actually integrated and sold to Czech merchants (Comgate, GoPay, Pays, GP webpay, Shoptet Pay, ThePay, BNPL, insurance). Listing pages carry install/rating signals and vendor descriptions, making it the cleanest buy-side adoption proxy in CZ e-commerce.

source_name: Shoptet Blog – Platební metody a platební brány (annual overview)
why_relevant: Vendor-neutral-ish annual roundup written for merchants, comparing CZ gateways, pricing models and feature sets; useful for tracking which providers the platform itself promotes and how the competitive set shifts year over year.

source_name: Kancelář finančního arbitra – Sbírka rozhodnutí (decisions collection)
why_relevant: The Czech financial ombudsman publishes anonymised nálezy/rozhodnutí naming the payment service provider complained against. These are the only public, adjudicated records of failing payment implementations (unauthorised transactions, SCA failures, card/gateway disputes) and directly expose vendor and bank weaknesses.

source_name: Kancelář finančního arbitra – Platební služby area page + annual reports
why_relevant: Scope/jurisdiction page and gateway to annual reports (výroční zprávy) which aggregate complaint counts by institution and dispute type — a quantitative buy-side complaint signal.
